_changes: hash_spec.normalize: states that lowercase happens BEFORE sort. Neon found the ambiguity. It is not a tie-break convention -- ASCII orders all uppercase before all lowercase, so sort-then-lowercase can emit a list that is NOT sorted. Latent on v1 because every entry is already lowercase; live the moment one arrives capitalised.

hash_spec.join: states newline is a SEPARATOR, not a terminator -- no trailing newline. Friday found it, Neon reproduced the alternative as 8b3345a7. Same roster, different string, from an unstated convention. Same shape as hex-vs-decimal.
_note: v2 changes the SPEC's precision, not the computation. The fingerprint is therefore UNCHANGED from v1 -- which is itself the check that nothing silently moved while the ambiguities were being closed.

hash_spec.normalize: lowercase each entry FIRST, then sort
hash_spec.join: newline as SEPARATOR between entries; no trailing newline
